document_title: The Chemical Professional's Code of Conduct
notes: Approved by ACS Council March 16, 1994; most recently updated August 28, 2019. Replaces The Chemist's Creed (1965). Covers obligations to public, science, profession, employers, students, and personal conduct.

document_title: RSC Code of Conduct and Guide to Ethics
notes: Binding on all RSC members at Associate Member grade and above; applicants must sign commitment on admission. References The Hague Ethical Guidelines. Separate Guide to Ethics provides detailed guidance.

document_title: Working Party on Ethics in Chemistry — Ethical Guidelines and Code of Chemical Ethos
notes: EuChemS Working Party elaborates codes of conduct and approaches to good scientific practice and chemical ethos. Covers internal (research integrity) and external (dual-use, sustainability, science policy) responsibilities.

organization: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry
document_title: IUPAC Guiding Principles of Responsible Chemistry
notes: Eight guiding principles for responsible chemistry: transparency, equity, accountability, sustainability, systems thinking, long-term impact, stakeholder engagement, ethical responsibility integration. Endorsed The Hague Ethical Guidelines in 2016.

organization: Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons
document_title: The Hague Ethical Guidelines
notes: Developed 2015 by OPCW-convened experts from 24 countries. Endorsed by IUPAC, ICCA, and ICTA. Focuses on dual-use awareness, peaceful applications, Chemical Weapons Convention compliance. Now referenced in RSC Code of Conduct.

document_title: Responsible Care — Guiding Principles and Codes of Management Practice
notes: Launched in US by ACC (then CMA) in 1988. Membership condition for all ACC members. Seven Codes of Management Practice covering community awareness, pollution prevention, process safety, distribution, employee health, product stewardship, security. CEO-level commitment required.

document_title: Responsible Care Europe — Voluntary Management Framework
notes: Cefic adopted Responsible Care in 1985. Developed voluntary Responsible Care Management Framework aligning to highest industry standards and sustainability principles. Membership condition for Cefic members.

document_title: Responsible Care Global Charter
notes: Established at 2006 International Conference on Chemicals Management. CEO-level commitment by signatory companies. 64 national chemical associations implement nationally. Global Product Strategy also launched at same time. Endorsed by IUPAC and ICTA.

organization: Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America
document_title: Code on Interactions with Health Care Professionals
notes: First published 2002; revised 2009, 2019, and 2022 (effective January 2022). Governs pharmaceutical company marketing to physicians. Prohibits entertainment, luxury venue events, direct gifts. Covers CME support, speaker programs, and consulting arrangements.

organization: International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers & Associations
document_title: IFPMA Code of Practice
notes: First created 1981; major revision 2019. Covers HCP interactions, gifts, CME, clinical trial transparency, and patient organization relationships. Includes prohibition on gifts to HCPs. Supplemented by Ethoscope open-source guidance resource.

organization: European Federation of Pharmaceutical Industries and Associations
document_title: EFPIA Code of Practice
notes: 2019 consolidated edition replaces separate codes on HCP promotion and patient organization interactions. Covers traditional and digital communications. Embodies IFPMA Code principles. Binding on EFPIA member companies.

organization: Association of the British Pharmaceutical Industry
document_title: Code of Practice for the Pharmaceutical Industry (2024 Edition)
notes: First adopted 1958; 2024 edition in force from 1 October 2024. Administered by the independent Prescription Medicines Code of Practice Authority (PMCPA). Covers prescription medicine promotion to HCPs, patient information, speaker programs, and transparency.

document_title: Code of Business Ethics
notes: Effective September 1, 2018; unanimously endorsed by AAM Board. Covers generic and biosimilar manufacturers. Distinctive for emphasizing patient access and market competition as ethical values. Covers medicine safety, HCP interactions, and clinical trials.

document_title: BIO Statement of Ethical Principles
notes: Adopted by BIO Board of Directors. Covers responsible biotechnology development, informed consent, health and safety priority, science-based regulation, and patient access. Supplemented by BIO Membership Compact & Social Responsibilities.

document_title: Code of Ethics and Publication Ethics Policy
notes: Covers members, journal authors, reviewers, and conference participants. Emphasizes research integrity (no fabrication, falsification, plagiarism), proper attribution, and non-discrimination. Includes investigation procedures for research misconduct.

document_title: Code of Ethics for Certified Welding Inspectors (QC1:2016) and Code of Conduct for Technical Committee Members
notes: QC1:2016-AMD1 governs all AWS-certified welding inspectors; public safety paramount. Separate Code of Conduct for Technical Committee Members covers committee participation standards. AWS QC1 certification widely required in US construction, aerospace, and manufacturing.

document_title: SME Code of Ethics
notes: Applies to all SME-certified professionals. Covers competence, honesty, non-discrimination, confidentiality, conflict of interest disclosure, and societal impact. Explicitly addresses public health, safety, conservation, and environmental issues in manufacturing.

document_title: RBA Code of Conduct (Version 8.0, 2024)
notes: Formerly Electronic Industry Citizenship Coalition (EICC). Founded 2004 by leading electronics companies. Version 8.0 effective January 2024. Five sections: Labor, Health & Safety, Environment, Management Systems, Business Ethics. Third-party audit-verified. 200+ member companies across electronics, retail, auto, toy sectors.

document_title: SEMI Code of Conduct
notes: Governs conduct within SEMI activities, events, and committees. Emphasizes professional, respectful working environment free from abuse and harassment. SEMI is the global industry association uniting the entire electronics manufacturing and design supply chain.

document_title: Voluntary Ethical Guidelines for Surveillance, Policing, and Semiconductors
notes: Addresses responsible semiconductor supply to prevent human rights abuses. Four areas: due diligence, customer relations, development/design, transparency/traceability. Focuses on preventing semiconductor technologies from enabling oppressive surveillance and policing.

document_title: SAE International Code of Ethical Conduct
notes: Last updated October 26, 2020. Applies to Board members, officers, members, volunteers, staff, vendors, and consultants. Requires lawful, ethical, professional conduct and respectful treatment. Prohibits illegal, dishonest, or unethical actions.

organization: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics
document_title: AIAA Code of Ethics
notes: Nearly 30,000 members from 91 countries. Key principles: public safety paramount, conflict of interest avoidance, zero tolerance of bribery/fraud, accurate technical reporting, respect and non-discrimination. Formal Ethics Committee with complaint process.

organization: International Forum on Business Ethical Conduct
document_title: Global Principles of Business Ethics for the Aerospace and Defence Industry
notes: Established 2009 by AIA (US) and ASD (Europe); forum launched 2010. Global Principles address: zero tolerance of corruption, use of advisors, conflicts of interest, proprietary information protection. Open to all aerospace/defense companies. Annual conference. 200+ member companies.

organization: Institute of Marine Engineering, Science and Technology
document_title: Rules of Professional Conduct
profession_name: Marine Engineer / Marine Scientist / Marine Technologist
notes: Binding on all members at Associate Member (AMIMarEST) grade and above. Covers: competence development, compliance with Royal Charter and bylaws, reporting of violations by other members, notification of criminal convictions. IMarEST is the world's largest multi-disciplinary marine professional body.

document_title: AdvaMed Code of Ethics on Interactions with Health Care Professionals (2022/2025 Edition)
notes: 2022 revision effective June 1, 2022; updated November 2025 to address data/AI responsibilities. Six cornerstone values: innovation, education, integrity, respect, responsibility, transparency. Covers HCP interactions, training, consulting, speaking arrangements. Includes crosswalk with PhRMA Code.

document_title: RJC Code of Practices (COP) 2024 Edition
notes: 2024 edition effective January 1, 2025 (supersedes 2019 edition). Mandatory for all RJC commercial members within 2 years of joining; third-party audited. Covers entire jewellery and watch supply chain: mine to retail. Addresses business ethics, human rights, labor, health/safety, environmental performance. Recognized by ICMM as equivalent standard for mining members.

organization: Ethical Supply Chain Program (formerly ICTI Ethical Toy Program, formerly ICTI CARE)
document_title: Code of Business Practices
notes: ICTI Code of Business Practices first established 1995; ICTI CARE Process launched 2002; became ICTI Ethical Toy Program 2018; rebranded Ethical Supply Chain Program 2024. Third-party audited. Covers ~70% of global toy production. Addresses child/forced labor, gender equity, working hours, wages, health/safety, and environmental sustainability.

organization: World Federation of the Sporting Goods Industry
document_title: WFSGI Code of Conduct — Guiding Principles
notes: Model Code of Conduct for sporting goods companies and their suppliers. Based on ILO Conventions and Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Covers forced/child labor, discrimination, freedom of association, wages, working hours, health/safety, and environmental compliance. Members encouraged to adopt own specific code built on these standards.
